If anyone is interested in a book on mnemonics I'd recommend Your Memory How It Works & How To Improve It, by Kenneth L. Higbee. Although he doesn't use them for numbers, Semiogogue has something on mnemonics.

Mnemonics for arithmetic, a subset of math - is what I tend to think of this as. It is pretty handy for working with some pretty large numbers in your head. I'm familiar with it but not a practitioner. I can usually do the small numbers in my head but don't really have a need to do more than that, if that makes any sense? If I'm shopping, I usually know the total and the tax amount. (In Maine, that's pretty simply 'cause it's just five percent on taxable goods.)

Fantastic stuff and a great way to impress people, I suppose. Another great way to get really good at doing some basic math in your head is to play AD&D 2nd Edition. Calculating THAC0 and the spell damage is actually a good way to get good at basic math in your head.

Lovely stuff!
